subject: history
title: Youth, Women and Workers Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll see how Nazis shaped boys, girls, mothers and factory workers.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Hitler Youth, BDM, women and the Labour Front.
final_note: You learned how the Nazis tried to mould every German into a loyal Volk member.

concepts.def: League of German Girls — fitness and motherhood
Children, kitchen, church — women's Nazi role
Medal for women with four or more children
KdF — workers' leisure trips and benefits
SdA — improved factory canteens and lighting

walkthroughs.body_html:
By 1936 Hitler Youth membership was compulsory for boys aged 10-18.

Boys did marching, camping and weapons drill. Girls in the BDM learnt fitness, cooking and racial duty. Schools rewrote textbooks: race studies, PE (15% of lessons) and a girls' 'home craft' track.

Women were pushed out of professions and back to the home.

The slogan was Kinder, Küche, Kirche — children, kitchen, church. Marriage loans rewarded large families. The Mother's Cross medal honoured women with 4, 6 or 8+ children — gold for 8.

Trade unions were banned in May 1933 and replaced by the German Labour Front.

Strength through Joy (KdF) offered cheap holidays, cinema and a 'people's car' — the Volkswagen Beetle (none delivered). Beauty of Labour improved canteens and lighting. Unemployment fell from 6 million to under 200,000 by 1939.

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.

mcqs.q: What was the political significance of the Reichstag Fire?
options: The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Hitler used it to issue the Reichstag Fire Decree suspending civil liberties, jail Communists, and create the conditions for the Enabling Act of March 1933.
Hitler personally set the fire and blamed it on the Communists.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.

mcqs.q: When did the systematic mass murder of Jews begin?
options: The killings only began after Germany lost the Battle of Stalingrad.
Mass shootings by Einsatzgruppen began with Operation Barbarossa in June 1941; industrial extermination camps followed from 1942.
The Holocaust began as soon as Hitler came to power in 1933.
The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
